findings.detail: Exit status 1 does not uniquely mean the ref is missing: Git also returns 1 without diagnostics when the ref exists but its commit object is unavailable. A read-only reproduction preserved origin/main while hiding its objects; the old resolver and caller stopped, but the new path returned an empty base and continued. If only the base object is missing, collection can therefore emit successful partial-coverage JSON instead of reporting the repository problem. Both canonical helper copies contain this handler.
findings.fix: Resolve the candidate ref without ^{commit} first, treating only an absent ref as optional. Once the ref exists, make every failure to validate its commit fatal, with the ref name and diagnostic. Apply the same change to review-until-clean's helper and cover an existing ref whose object is missing.
findings.title: write-bash-scripts: Checked commands: Missing base objects are treated as absent refs.
